flashcards.front: What condition makes a process safe to advance to the next simulated round?
flashcards.back: It must have the evidence required by the synchronizer that current-round communication and acknowledgements are complete.

flashcards.front: Why does the simple synchronizer use dummy messages?
flashcards.back: A dummy message preserves the one-message-per-neighbor assumption, so its arrival can signal completion even when there is no payload.

flashcards.front: What assumption does the $\alpha$ synchronizer remove?
flashcards.back: It removes the fixed one-message-per-neighbor assumption and instead tracks when the current-round communication is complete.

homework.prompt: Trace a simple synchronizer round on a three-process graph where one process has no payload to send to a neighbor.
homework.rubric: Insert the dummy message, show which messages or acknowledgements are observed, and identify the safe-to-proceed point.

homework.prompt: Explain why the $\alpha$ synchronizer needs a different completion argument from the simple synchronizer.
homework.rubric: State the removed fixed-message assumption and describe the evidence needed before a process advances.
